summary: All 27 occurrences checked. Active change/exchange combines an ordinary object, a b-marked exchanged item, or an indexed person with a b-marked counterpart. Ring exchange can also have ʕam ḥḏoḏe as partner.

Objectless active mbadli (PrS 17/19) marks iterative alternation; this differs formally from ruḥo-reflexive disguising and from Detransitive change. The one-token subsense remains open to an elliptical-object analysis.

Detransitive change covers situation, attitudes, officeholder and shape. At 3/65 the skin-colour comparison can describe variation across people, not a temporal transformation of one person. At 8/11 Part. Pass. describes changeability, already present in the entry.

The supplied eye-shape quotation cites both 3/21 and 3/65, but only 3/21 supplies that wording. The new 3/65 example preserves the different skin-colour clause; detach its misleading citation from the old eye-shape text.

No duplicate examples added for 23/45, 24/35–36, 24/155, 24/201, 26/110, 26/140, 62/261 or the established Detransitive witnesses. The existing clothing passage and PrS 36/33 overlap despite different legacy reference formats; no unverified citation conversion made.
Active objectless turn-taking and active replacement of an overt person coexist in Jan 1.15/581; they should not be conflated with the Detransitive merely because replacement is mutual.

Jan supplies active Infectum-wa absent in the baseline and round 1, including habitual clothing change and counterfactual/past possibility in Jan 4.II/958, 978. A -wa form does not by itself imply repetition.

General ruḥo self-change at Jan 4.II/896 overturns round 1’s restriction of II.2 to disguise. Existing disguise examples remain valid; the broader gloss now covers both uses. The learned discussion of magazine design and political/social roles also makes static Part. Pass. difference particularly clear.
Jan Beṯ-Şawoce English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses rest on the Turoyo; any English quoted below is copied from that supplied translation.

A person can stand as the object of changing clothes: mother mbadəlali after the narrator’s clothes became soaked. This changes the affected participant expression, not the lexical clothing-change meaning.
Successive bearer replacements supply independent support for the round-1 objectless abwechseln subsense and add its Infectum-wa cell. Overt u ḥreno and -nne in the same passage remain sense 1.
Officer replacement and social-role change extend the round-1 Detransitive change sense to administration and social debate; no new numbered transfer sense is necessary.
